newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia sets up state-owned airline.
newsitem.headline: Georgia sets up state-owned airline.

text.p: Georgia's first state airline carrier GAO Georgian Airlines has begun domestic and international flights, the transport minister said.

Merab Adeishvili told Reuters the company would operate Russian-made Tupolev and Yakovlev aircraft which, although always belonging to the government, had until recently been leased by the private carrier Orbi who has gone bankrupt.
He did not say how many planes the company would operate.
Adeishvili also said Georgia and Airbus Industrie had reached agreement to lease two A-320 jets soon.
"Initially we planned to lease two A-310 aircraft, but later decided to lease two 155-seat A-320s," he said, adding that a final agreement was expected by the end of this month.
Adeishvili said that the new airline needed financial help.
"I do not rule out that in the future a bank or an investor will appear which will give a loan to Georgian Airlines if it has state guarantees," he said.
There are 13 private airlines registered in Georgia. - Margarita Antidze, Tbilisi Newsroom +995 32 983 961
